targetTexts.2: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
targetTexts.3: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
targetTexts.4: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
targetTexts.5: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
targetTexts.6: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
targetTexts.7: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
targetTexts.8: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
targetTexts.9: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
targetTexts.10: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
targetTexts.11: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
targetTexts.12: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
targetTexts.13: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
targetTexts.14: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
targetTexts.15: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
targetTexts.16: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
targetTexts.17: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
targetTexts.18: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
targetTexts.19: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him?
targetTexts.20: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
targetTexts.21: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
targetTexts.22: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
targetTexts.23: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
targetTexts.24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
targetTexts.25: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
targetTexts.26: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
targetTexts.27: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’
targetTexts.28: I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
targetTexts.29: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
targetTexts.30: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
targetTexts.31: then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
targetTexts.32: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
targetTexts.33: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
targetTexts.34: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
targetTexts.35: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.
